name: Breadcrumbs
purpose: Secondary navigation showing the user's location within the site hierarchy and letting them step back to ancestor pages. A row of breadcrumb levels (links) separated by a divider, ending in the current page (a non-link).

props.name: state
props.$note: Per .Breadcrumb level. 'no-link' = the current/last item (non-clickable). Hover and Pressed share a single combined state.

variants.name: default
variants.use: A clickable ancestor level (Small Print Link, font-6 regular).

variants.name: hover-pressed
variants.use: Interactive feedback for a level on hover/press. Shares text colour with default — differentiated by link styling (e.g. underline), not colour.

variants.name: no-link
variants.use: The current page — the final crumb, rendered as plain Small Print (non-link).

tokens.separator: A '/' (forward slash) text character between levels, in the same text/default + font-6 styling (confirmed by Dave). Not an icon.

accessibility.focus: When tabbed to, every focusable level must show a visible outline; use default native focus states
accessibility.targetArea: Each level has a defined target area (spec shows per-level target/focus areas); confirm min 44×44 where applicable
accessibility.structure: REVIEW (inferred): mark up as a nav landmark labelled 'Breadcrumb' with an ordered list; current page exposed via aria-current='page' (matches the 'no-link' state)

antiPatterns: REVIEW (inferred): making the current page (no-link) a clickable link
REVIEW (inferred): relying on colour alone to show the hover/pressed state — here states share text/default (#333333), so a non-colour cue (underline) is required (see WCAG state-contrast guidance)
REVIEW (inferred): using breadcrumbs as the primary navigation rather than a secondary location aid

tokenValidation.against: token store re-based on Figma native variable export
tokenValidation.notes: All three states bind text/default (#333333) at font-6 regular; no colour differentiation between default / hover-pressed / no-link. State differentiation relies on link styling (underline) + interactivity, not colour. Hover and Pressed are a single combined state — per the WCAG state-contrast rule, active/pressed normally warrants stronger differentiation than hover; flag for review. specs/* annotation styles ignored.
